entities.summary: Frederick Hugh "Old Eagle Eyes" Lehman was a Canadian professional ice hockey player. A goaltender, he started his ice hockey career playing for the Pembroke Lumber Kings and the Berlin Dutchmen. In 1911, Lehman joined the New Westminster Royals, playing for the Royals for three seasons, before joining the Vancouver Millionaires in 1914. Lehman played half of his 22-year professional career with Vancouver, winning his only Stanley Cup; he would be unsuccessful in seven other attempts. In 1926, he joined the Chicago Black Hawks of the National Hockey League (NHL), playing a full season and splitting the second one as player and head coach.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hughie Lehman's Stanley Cup win with Vancouver Millionaires in 1914 marked a significant regional achievement in Canadian hockey history. His seven attempts to repeat this feat demonstrate his enduring impact on the sport.
